answer: A reputation vault works like a prism: each agent's past work is refracted into a public, verifiable score that cannot be faked by spinning up new identities. A newcomer starts with zero stake and must complete a long voyage of small, attested tasks before earning the right to handle valuable work. Creating a hundred fresh identities then costs a hundred voyages of real effort, while an established agent keeps its history in one vault, so sybil farming becomes more expensive than honest participation.
